saints.name: St. Martin of Braga
saints.title: Bishop, Apostle of the Suevi
saints.shortBlurb: A monk from Pannonia who converted the Suevi of Galicia from Arianism and became archbishop of Braga…
biography: Born in Pannonia about 520, Martin became a monk on a pilgrimage to the Holy Land, and about 550 sailed to Gallaecia in the northwest of Spain, then ruled by the Arian Suevi. Near their capital at Braga he founded the monastery of Dumium and was made its bishop.

By his preaching King Miro and the Suevic people were won from Arianism to the Catholic faith. Martin sat in the First Council of Braga in 561 and, raised to the metropolitan see of Braga, presided over the Second in 572, which received his collection of eighty-four canons translated from the Greek.

Gregory of Tours judged him second to none in the learning of his age. He adapted Seneca in moral treatises, the "Formula Vitae Honestae," dedicated to King Miro, and "De Ira"; he translated the Sayings of the Egyptian Fathers from the Greek, and in "De Correctione Rusticorum" taught the bishops how to root out rural superstition.

He died about 580 and was buried at Dumium, the monastery he had founded. Posterity named him Apostle of the Suevi; and so exactly did his "Formula Vitae Honestae" follow Seneca that it was long mistaken for the philosopher's own work.
saints.knownFor: Converting the Suevi and reforming the Church of Galicia.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
